c.tagline: Mexico's colonial jewel of Talavera-tiled facades, baroque churches and the birthplace of mole poblano.

taxi.fareNote: Street taxis are metered but many drivers quote a flat price, so agree the fare before setting off; ride-hail apps (Uber, DiDi) are widely used, usually cheaper and considered safer, and the RUTA BRT covers the main corridors.

emergency.note: 911 is Mexico's unified emergency number for police, fire and ambulance; 089 is the anonymous tip line and 078 the national tourist assistance line.

solo.f: Safety index is the main factor (45/100)

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the centre; caution at night

hoods: Barrio del Alto / Paseo San Francisco
hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed colonial core around the zocalo, the twin-towered Puebla Cathedral, the tiled Casa de los Muñecos and dozens of baroque churches, its streets clad in blue-and-white Talavera; a dense, walkable grid of plazas, museums and mole restaurants that is best for first-timers who want the main sights on foot.

The modern, prosperous district southwest of downtown built around the Angelopolis malls, the Estrella de Puebla observation wheel and the Amparo-linked cultural venues, ringed by high-rise hotels and business towers; best for shopping, contemporary dining and a car-friendly stay.

The revitalised riverside strip around Paseo San Francisco and the Barrio del Alto, where old textile factories now house design hotels, craft-beer bars, museums and restaurants beside the San Francisco church; a stylish, lively base for evenings out.

The university town 8 km west, crowned by the Great Pyramid of Cholula topped with a hilltop church and framed by Popocatepetl; its plazas, mezcal bars and student energy make it a laid-back, nightlife-heavy alternative to central Puebla.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water, as everywhere in Mexico.

transit.hours: The RUTA BRT lines and city buses (rutas/colectivos) run roughly 05:00 to 23:00, with limited late-night service filled by taxis and ride apps.
transit.note: Puebla's backbone is the RUTA bus rapid transit; ordinary microbuses (rutas/colectivos) fan out across the city, while ride-hail apps and taxis handle door-to-door and late-night trips. The compact Centro Historico is best explored on foot.
transit.pay: The RUTA BRT uses a rechargeable smart card tapped at station turnstiles; a single ride is about MXN 8.50 (~US$0.45). Ordinary city microbuses are paid in cash to the driver.

tip.r: Around 10-15% at restaurants is customary; rounding up for taxis and leaving small change for hotel and bar staff is appreciated.

food.name: Cemita poblana
food.desc: Sesame-crusted brioche-like roll piled with milanesa or carnitas, quesillo, avocado, papalo herb and chipotle; Puebla's great sandwich.

places.name: Cemitas Aguilar

places.note: Long-running local chain that many poblanos rate as the best arabes in town.

places.name: Tacos Bagdad

food.desc: Convent sweets: candied sweet-potato camotes, tortitas de Santa Clara and borrachitos, sold along the Calle de los Dulces.

places.name: Dulceria de Santa Clara

food.name: Pasita
food.desc: Sticky raisin liqueur served as a shot with a cube of fresh cheese and a raisin on a stick, a ritual unique to Puebla.

landmarks: Puebla Cathedral
A majestic 16th- and 17th-century cathedral whose 69-metre bell towers, the tallest in Mexico, preside grandly over the UNESCO-listed historic centre.
Capilla del Rosario (Rosary Chapel)
A dazzling Baroque chapel inside Santo Domingo church, dripping with 23-karat gold leaf and once hailed as the eighth wonder of the world.
Zócalo de Puebla
The arcaded main square shaded by old trees and ringed by cafés, where poblanos stroll past fountains beneath the cathedral's towering silhouette.
Biblioteca Palafoxiana
Founded in 1646 as the first public library in the Americas, it shelters 45,000 antique volumes on magnificently carved cedar shelves.
Museo Amparo
One of Mexico's finest museums, pairing exceptional pre-Hispanic artefacts with colonial and contemporary art inside two beautifully restored viceregal buildings.
Fuertes de Loreto y Guadalupe
Hilltop forts where Mexican forces defeated the French army on 5 May 1862, the victory celebrated worldwide every Cinco de Mayo.
Callejón de los Sapos
A cobbled alley painted in candy colours, packed with antiques dealers, weekend flea-market stalls and cantinas echoing with live mariachi.
Great Pyramid of Cholula
An easy day trip to the world's largest pyramid by volume, crowned by a golden-domed church with Popocatépetl volcano looming photogenically behind.
Mercado El Parián
Puebla's classic crafts market since 1801, the best hunting ground for hand-painted Talavera pottery, textiles and sweet camotes.
Estrella de Puebla
An 80-metre observation wheel that once held a Guinness record, offering sweeping sunset views over the city and its snow-capped volcanoes.

train.note: Puebla has no intercity passenger rail; a weekend tourist train runs the short hop to Cholula and all long-distance travel is by coach or car. Mexico's national network here carries freight only, and the nearest real passenger service is the El Insurgente commuter line between Mexico City and Toluca.

bus.note: No international coaches. CAPU, the main terminal north of the centre, is one of Mexico's busiest: ADO (https://www.ado.com.mx/) and Estrella Roja run to Mexico City every few minutes (about 2 hours), plus Oaxaca, Veracruz and direct services to both Mexico City airport terminals, which is a popular way to skip the capital entirely.

ferry.note: Puebla is inland on the central highlands between volcanoes, with no navigable water, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Africam Safari
half.blurb: A well-regarded drive-through safari park with free-roaming lions, giraffes and rhinos, about 30 minutes southeast of the city.

half.name: Atlixco
half.blurb: A colourful 'Pueblo Magico' known for flower nurseries, colonial streets and volcano views, about 30 km southwest.

full.name: Cantona
full.blurb: A vast, little-visited pre-Hispanic city with hundreds of ball courts and cobbled causeways, roughly 1.5 hours northeast.

full.name: Popocatepetl & Iztaccihuatl (Paso de Cortes)
full.blurb: Alpine trails and lookouts on the saddle between Mexico's two great volcanoes, a scenic full day west of the city.

laundry.note: Attended lavanderias dominate; self-service exists in cities
